learn.title: Regions, region pairs, sovereign regions, availability zones, datacenters
objectives: Describe how Azure datacenters, availability zones, regions and geographies fit together.
Choose a region using latency, data residency, service availability and price.
Explain what region pairs provide and their limits.
Describe sovereign regions: Azure Government and Azure operated by 21Vianet.
Tell zonal services from zone-redundant services.
concepts: Datacenter
A Microsoft facility with racks of servers, power, cooling and networking. Customers can't access datacenters directly and never choose one.
Availability zone
One or more datacenters inside a region with independent power, cooling and networking. Regions that support zones have at least three.
Region
A geographic area with one or more datacenters linked by a low-latency network. Most resources are deployed to a region.
Geography
A discrete market, usually a country, containing two or more regions, which preserves data residency and compliance boundaries.
Region pair

Two regions in the same geography (with rare exceptions), usually hundreds of miles apart. Updates roll out to one region of the pair at a time, and recovery of one region per pair is prioritised in a broad outage.
Non-paired region
Many newer regions have no pair and rely on availability zones for resilience instead.
Zonal service
A resource pinned to one zone that you choose, such as a VM, a managed disk or a zonal public IP.
Zone-redundant service
A service that spreads itself across zones automatically, such as zone-redundant storage (ZRS).
Non-regional (global) service
A service not tied to one region, such as Microsoft Entra ID, Azure DNS and Azure Front Door.
Sovereign region
An Azure instance isolated from global Azure for legal or compliance reasons: Azure Government (US public sector) and Azure operated by 21Vianet (China).
comparisons: Zones protect against a datacenter failure inside a region. A second region protects against a whole-region outage.
Zonal: you place it in one zone and add redundancy yourself. Zone-redundant: the platform replicates across zones for you.
Region pair vs any second region
Pairs add staggered updates, prioritised recovery and the GRS target. Tools such as Azure Site Recovery can use any region.
Sovereign regions have separate portals, separate identity and screened operators, and some services differ.
traps: Not every region supports availability zones, and not every region has a pair.
A pair isn't always two-way, and a few pairs cross geographies (Brazil South is paired with South Central US).
Availability zones are inside one region; they aren't separate regions.
Service availability and prices can differ between regions.
Zone numbers are logical per subscription, so zone 1 in one subscription might be a different physical zone from zone 1 in another.
revision: Zone-enabled regions have at least three zones.
Two or more VMs across two or more zones: 99.99% VM SLA.
Region pairs: same geography, staggered updates, recovery priority, GRS secondary.
Sovereign: Azure Government (US) and Azure operated by 21Vianet (China).
Choose regions for latency, residency, service availability and cost.

opts: One VM in each of two subscriptions
Two or more VMs across availability zones
A single VM with standard HDD disks
Two or more VMs in an availability set

questions.on: Describe availability zones
questions.q: A company needs its app to survive a datacenter failure but has a limited budget and no requirement to survive a full regional outage. Which approach fits best?
opts: Deploy full copies in three regions
Deploy across availability zones in one region
Use a sovereign region
Use a single VM with a premium disk

questions.on: Describe Azure regions, region pairs, and sovereign regions
questions.q: A storage account in a paired region uses GRS. How is its secondary region determined?
opts: It's always a region on another continent
The customer picks any region at random each day
It's the region closest to the administrator
It's the primary region's paired region, determined by Azure

questions.on: Describe availability zones
questions.q: Which statement describes the physical placement of availability zones in a region?
opts: They're separate floors of the same building
They're in different countries
They're physically separate locations, far enough apart to reduce shared risks but close enough for low-latency connections
They're the same datacenter with different names

questions.on: Describe Azure regions, region pairs, and sovereign regions
questions.q: When might a company choose a disaster-recovery region other than its region's pair?
opts: Never, because Azure blocks replication to unpaired regions
Only when using locally redundant storage
Only when the company has no subscription
When the paired region lacks a service it needs, or another region better fits its latency or compliance needs

questions.on: Describe Azure regions, region pairs, and sovereign regions
questions.q: Some Azure regions don't appear for most customers. Which explanation is accurate?
opts: They're visible only to Microsoft employees
Some regions are restricted, for example to customers with in-country needs, and are often used for in-country disaster recovery
Those regions have been deleted
They appear only in the free account

questions.on: Describe Azure regions, region pairs, and sovereign regions
questions.q: An app tier in one region queries a database hosted in a distant region thousands of times per page. Pages are slow. What's the best fix?
opts: Add more tags to the database
Switch the database to locally redundant storage
Place the app tier and database in the same region
Use a larger VM in the distant region

questions.on: Describe availability zones
questions.q: A team plans a zone-redundant deployment, but the zone options are greyed out for their chosen region. What should they do?
opts: Create more resource groups in the same region
Choose a region that supports availability zones, if their other requirements allow it
Open a support ticket to have zones added to that region immediately
Switch the VMs to a different operating system

questions.on: Describe Azure datacenters
questions.q:
Evaluate these statements.
1. Customers choose which datacenter building hosts their resources.
2. An availability zone consists of one or more datacenters.
3. A zone-enabled region contains multiple zones, each made of datacenters.
Which statements are true?
opts: Statement 1 only
Statements 1, 2 and 3
Statements 2 and 3 only
Statements 1 and 2 only

questions.on: Describe Azure regions, region pairs, and sovereign regions
questions.q: A company serves users worldwide, but EU customers' data must stay in the EU and the EU service must survive a datacenter failure. Which design fits best?
opts: Copy EU data to every region worldwide for speed
Store EU customer data in a zone-enabled EU region with zone-redundant deployment, and serve other users from regions near them
Store all data in one US region with LRS
Store EU data in a sovereign US region

questions.on: Describe availability zones
questions.q: Can every Azure service be deployed to every Azure region?
opts: Yes, every service launches in every region at the same time
No, resources can only be deployed in the region where the subscription was created
Yes, but only for customers with a premium support plan
No. Service availability varies by region, so check that a service is offered in the region you choose

questions.on: Describe availability zones
questions.q: A web tier runs on VMs in three availability zones, yet the whole app went down when zone 2 failed. What's the most likely cause?
opts: The region pair was updating at the same time
Availability zones can't protect web servers
A dependency, such as the database, was deployed as a single zonal resource in zone 2
The VMs needed tags for zone protection

questions.on: Describe Azure regions, region pairs, and sovereign regions
questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a benefit of Azure region pairs?
opts: Staggered rollout of planned updates
Prioritised recovery of one region per pair in a broad outage
A predefined secondary region for geo-redundant storage
Automatic failover of every customer VM to the paired region with no configuration

questions.on: Describe availability zones
questions.q: Storage data must stay available if a zone fails and must also be recoverable if the whole primary region fails. Which redundancy option fits best?
opts: Locally redundant storage (LRS)
Zone-redundant storage (ZRS)
Geo-zone-redundant storage (GZRS)
A single managed disk
questions.e: GZRS combines ZRS in the primary region with geo-replication to the secondary region.

questions.on: Describe Azure regions, region pairs, and sovereign regions
questions.q: A company runs its app in global Azure and now must serve customers inside mainland China from in-country infrastructure. What's the most appropriate approach?
opts: Add a China region to the existing global subscription
Serve China from a European region pair
Use Azure Government for the China workload
Deploy a separate instance in Azure operated by 21Vianet with its own account, and manage it alongside the global deployment

questions.on: Describe Azure regions, region pairs, and sovereign regions
questions.q:
Evaluate these statements.
1. Azure Government is physically isolated from global Azure.
2. Any organisation can sign up for Azure Government.
3. Azure in mainland China is operated by 21Vianet.
Which statements are true?
opts: Statements 2 and 3 only
Statements 1 and 3 only
Statements 1 and 2 only
Statement 2 only

questions.on: Describe Azure regions, region pairs, and sovereign regions
questions.q: A company fails over a GRS storage account to its secondary region after a regional disaster. What risk should it expect?
opts: The data is moved to locally redundant storage in the failed region
No data can ever be lost with any redundancy option
Some of the most recent writes may be lost, because geo-replication is asynchronous
All data written in the last year is lost

questions.on: Describe Azure regions, region pairs, and sovereign regions
questions.q: An app's users are mostly in Japan, its data must remain in Japan, and it must survive a datacenter failure. Which region choice fits best?
opts: Azure Government
A region in Japan that supports availability zones
A Japanese region without availability zones, using a single VM
A region in Australia with availability zones
